subject.title: member-info fails with "fetch failed" on WSL2 in 2026.6.1 (SSRF fetch guard / undici dispatcher regression)

question: Should Teams Graph keep using the current guarded Microsoft Graph fetch path and repair WSL2/Undici behavior inside it, or should Teams Graph move to a different approved egress boundary?
rationale: The remaining choice affects OpenClaw's SSRF/DNS-pinning boundary and cannot be made safely from source-only evidence without live WSL2 Graph proof and maintainer security intent.

options.title: Live-reproduce and repair guarded fetch
options.body: Reproduce member-info on WSL2 with redacted Graph logs, then fix the existing guarded fetch or dispatcher behavior while preserving the SSRF boundary.

options.title: Fold into egress refactor
options.body: Keep this issue open but let the broader HTTP egress refactor own it only after that PR becomes mergeable and has Teams Graph-specific proof.

options.title: Accept WSL2 limitation
options.body: Document the limitation and leave the current guarded Graph path unchanged, accepting that affected WSL2 Teams member-info users must downgrade or avoid the action.

recommendation.title: Live-reproduce and repair guarded fetch
recommendation.body: Reproduce member-info on WSL2 with redacted Graph logs, then fix the existing guarded fetch or dispatcher behavior while preserving the SSRF boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest current owner signal for the guarded dispatcher and security-boundary choice because of PR #61777 merge and adjacent transport commits.
